notes: AXON is law enforcement tech (TASER CEDs, body cameras, Evidence.com cloud, drone counter-UAS via Dedrone). The 10-K narrative is dominated by U.S. state/local/federal law enforcement; explicit Pentagon Program Element or DoD program-of-record exposure is not material. The filing language mentions 'foreign governments' and 'major defense acquisition programs' only in generic governmental-regulation risk-factor boilerplate, not as material revenue. Most claims here will be UNVERIFIABLE under the J-Book lens (NOT_FOUND in a J-Book corpus that is RDT&E/Procurement focused) because the company does not name PE numbers or DoD programs of record. We extract a mix of (a) the few quasi-DoD-adjacent claims for J-Book testing and (b) standard non-J-Book control claims (acquisitions, customer concentration, facilities, counterparty).

claims.claim_text: Axon's primary customer vertical is U.S. federal, state and local law enforcement agencies; the company has customer relationships with a substantial number of such agencies.
claims.subject: Axon Enterprise
claims.object_value: U.S. federal, state and local law enforcement
claims.source_quote: Our largest customer vertical is U.S. federal, state and local law enforcement. Axon has a customer relationship with a substantial number of federal, state and local law enforcement agencies in the United States.

claims.claim_text: Axon expects U.S. government review of major defense acquisition programs and notes that cancellation of programs in which it provides products or services could materially affect it.
claims.subject: Axon Enterprise
claims.source_quote: Among the actions directed is a review of major defense acquisition programs that are more than 15% behind schedule or over budget, including identifying any programs for potential cancellation. Should the U.S. government review one or more major defense programs in which we provide products and/or services, and such review leads to a full or partial cancellation of one of these programs, it could have an adverse effect...

claims.claim_text: Axon derives a significant portion of revenue from TASER conducted-energy devices (CEDs); TASER revenue was $913.9M in FY2025 (32.9% of net sales).
claims.subject: Axon TASER product line

claims.claim_text: Axon's Personal Sensors line (primarily body cameras and Signal Sidearm) generated $397.0M in FY2025 revenue (14.2% of net sales).
claims.subject: Axon Personal Sensors (body cameras)
claims.source_quote: Personal Sensors (2) 397,035 14.2 316,938 15.2 80,097 25.3 ... 'Personal Sensors' primarily includes body cameras and accessories, signal sidearm, and related extended warranties.

claims.claim_text: Axon acquired Dedrone on October 1, 2024 for ~$391.1M incremental consideration, positioning Axon in airspace security / counter-UAS markets.
claims.subject: Dedrone (Axon subsidiary)
claims.source_quote: On October 1, 2024, we acquired the remaining 79.8% equity interests in Dedrone, a global leader in air space security, for incremental consideration transferred of approximately $391.1 million.

claims.claim_text: Axon acquired Carbyne Ltd. in February 2026 for $625M base price, a cloud-native emergency communications and response platform aimed at 911/next-gen public safety communications.
claims.subject: Carbyne (Axon subsidiary)
claims.source_quote: In February 2026, we acquired Carbyne Ltd. (Carbyne), a leading cloud-native emergency communications and response platform for a base purchase price of $625.0 million...

claims.claim_text: Axon maintains cybersecurity/cloud certifications including FedRAMP, CJIS, SOC 2, ISO and NIST — supporting sales to U.S. federal government customers.
claims.subject: Axon cloud security certifications
claims.source_quote: We maintain a formal cybersecurity and information security program that incorporates recommendations from recognized frameworks and standards, including ISO, SOC 2, CJIS, FedRAMP, and NIST.

claims.claim_text: Axon's primary headquarters spans seven facilities and ~900,000 sq ft in Phoenix, Arizona metro with manufacturing and research located in Arizona.
claims.subject: Axon Arizona headquarters
claims.object_value: ~900,000 sq ft in Phoenix, AZ metro
claims.source_quote: Our primary corporate headquarters are spread across seven facilities and approximately 900,000 square feet in the Phoenix, Arizona metropolitan area.

claims.claim_text: Axon and Dedrone are co-defendants in a patent-infringement suit by Airspace Systems involving certain drone technology; PTAB instituted IPR review of all three asserted patents on October 8, 2025.
claims.subject: Airspace Systems vs Axon/Dedrone
claims.object_value: PTAB IPR instituted Oct 8 2025; decision due by Oct 8 2026
claims.source_quote: Pending in the Eastern District of Virginia (Case No. 1:24-CV-01625) is a patent infringement suit filed by Airspace Systems, Inc. (Airspace) against Dedrone involving certain drone technology... On October 8, 2025, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board granted our petitions and instituted review on all claims of all three asserted patents.

claims.claim_text: Axon's auditor PwC identified a material weakness in internal controls over revenue recognition for customer contracts as of December 31, 2025.
claims.subject: Axon internal control over financial reporting
claims.object_value: material weakness in revenue recognition controls
claims.source_quote: the Company did not maintain, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025... a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting existed as of that date as the Company did not design and maintain effective controls related to revenue recognition for its customer contracts.
